extracted.intended_audience: research mathematicians in number theory/arithmetic geometry, especially those familiar with Mochizuki's IUTT and the abc/Vojta problems
extracted.subtask_description: A focused critique checklist for verifying the key logical and definitional steps in Mochizuki's Inter-universal Teichmüller Theory (IUTT) approach to the abc conjecture, highlighting where identifications, scalings, and indeterminacies must be controlled. Intended to guide mathematicians checking whether an asserted derivation of Vojta/abc from IUTT is valid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive uniform Vojta inequality (Conjecture 3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Show for a smooth geometrically connected curve X/k with ω_X(D) ample, and for all points P ∈ X(¯k) with [κ(P):Q] ≤ d, the inequality h_{ω_X(D)}(P) < (1+ε) d(P) + n1_D(P) + O(1) holds (equation (1.1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The abc-conjecture is treated as the special case P1_Q with D = 0+1+∞. A valid proof must produce the uniform Vojta inequality (1.1) with the O(1) constant depending only on ε,d,X, and show how this inequality is obtained from the IUTT constructions or reductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reduction to elliptic-curve/moduli-stack (Mell) setup
rubrics_metrics.description: Correctly reduce the Vojta inequality for X to an inequality on the moduli stack of elliptic curves Mell via Belyi maps and Frey-curve constructions, and account for all exceptional cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The reduction requires handling local data at places above 2 and ∞ (which must belong to a compact set) and possibly passing to scalar extensions so that elliptic curves acquire split semistable reduction everywhere. Exceptional 'sparse' lists (e.g., CM curves, lack of a core) must be treated separately and bounded uniformly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control of local data and split semistable reduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Ensure that (1) local data at places above 2 and ∞ lie in a compact set so infinite-place contributions are bounded, and (2) after possible scalar extension the elliptic curve E/k has split semistable reduction everywhere so Tate uniformization applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This permits expressing the relevant height h(P) in terms of deg(q_E) plus acceptable error terms (e.g., h(P)=1/6 deg(q_E)+O(h(P)^{1/2}+1) as in (1.2)). Any proof relying on these equalities must justify the boundedness and uniformity of the neglected contributions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of a prime ℓ with specified properties
rubrics_metrics.description: For each elliptic curve instance one must find a prime ℓ = ℓ(P) satisfying (i) size bounds relating ℓ to h(P) (inequalities like (1.3)), (ii) surjectivity-type condition: mod-ℓ Galois representation image contains SL_2(F_ℓ), and (iii) local non-splitting condition at bad places: the local Tate-extension class given by q_v is not an ℓ-th power.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These three properties are required to set up the IUTT arithmetic inputs. A valid proof must either produce such ℓ uniformly (with explicit dependence on d) or explain how finitely many exceptions are handled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Derive Claim 6 inequality (control of deg(q_E))
rubrics_metrics.description: Produce functions α_d(ℓ), β_d(ℓ) with α_d(ℓ) → 0 as ℓ → ∞ and β_d(ℓ) = O_d(1) such that deg(q_E) ≤ (1+α_d(ℓ))(d(P)+n1_∞(P)) + β_d(ℓ)·ℓ (as in Claim 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The chain of inequalities from IUTT must legitimately produce Claim 6: in particular, the transition from the IUTT arithmetic inequalities to an upper bound on deg(q_E) must be justified, with all error terms tracked and shown to be of the stated form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct meaning and definitions of |log(q)| and |log(Θ)|
rubrics_metrics.description: Precisely define the symbols appearing in the central inequality −|log(q)| ≤ −|log(Θ)| (equation (1.4)), interpreting them as the correct arithmetic/Arakelov degrees (e.g., −|log(q)| = −(1/(2ℓ)) deg(q_E)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because these symbols have specialized, non-naïve meanings in IUTT, any derivation using (1.4) must supply clear definitions and show that the algebraic manipulations of these objects legitimately correspond to the asserted numerical inequalities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include correct j^2 scaling for Θ-pilot to concrete Θ-data
rubrics_metrics.description: When relating the abstract Θ-pilot object to the arithmetic degrees of concrete Θ-pilot objects, include the necessary scaling by j^2 (the j-th concrete Θ-pilot object has degree j^2 times the q-pilot degree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper emphasizes that the identification from abstract Θ-pilot to concrete Θ-data requires scaling by j^2 (or an appropriate averaging). Failure to include this scalar results in an incorrect numerical comparison; therefore the proof must either include the j^2 factors consistently or justify an averaging/normalization that neutralizes them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consistent identifications of ordered 1-dimensional R-vector spaces
rubrics_metrics.description: Track and fix identifications among all copies of ordered 1-dimensional real vector spaces appearing (e.g., R_{Θ}^{(12)}, R_{q}^{(12)}, the copies for concrete pilot objects, and the standard real numbers R_Θ and R_q) in a globally consistent way before comparing numerical degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The critique shows that inconsistent or monodromic identifications (for instance introducing scalars on one side only) yield contradictions or force omission of crucial scaling factors. A valid proof must provide an explicit and consistent scheme of identifications so numerical inequalities are meaningful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain clear distinction between abstract and concrete pilot objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Avoid conflating abstract pilot objects (elements of R^{(12)} encoding abstract data) with concrete pilot objects (actual elements built from q_v ∈ ō_{k_v} whose Arakelov degrees are concrete numbers) without proving that the abstract→concrete passage preserves the required numerical information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholze–Stix stress that Mochizuki's work does not properly distinguish these, leading to an asserted identification of concrete Θ- and q-pilot objects up to indeterminacies. Any valid argument must either make this distinction precise or provide a theorem that the abstract equality implies the concrete equality up to quantitatively controlled error.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control and quantitatively bound indeterminacies ('blurring')
rubrics_metrics.description: All indeterminacies arising from poly-isomorphisms, choices in the multiradial algorithm, log-links/Θ-links, or averaging procedures must be bounded explicitly and shown to be small enough to preserve the desired inequalities (not of magnitude O(ℓ^2) or otherwise large enough to obliterate the inequality).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors report Mochizuki's claim that 'blurring' by indeterminacies makes diagrams commute; a valid proof must replace vague 'blurring' by explicit, small error bounds so that key inequalities remain non-vacuous.

rubrics_metrics.name: Justify use of Θ-link and log-link isomorphisms (canonicity and effect)
rubrics_metrics.description: When using Θ-links or log-links between Hodge theaters, provide a canonical or otherwise controlled choice of isomorphism and show precisely how these links transport pilot objects and associated numerical data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The paper notes there's a 'canonical choice' of Θ-link via the common generator of the monoid N, but also that Mochizuki works with full poly-isomorphisms. A correct derivation must explain why any non-uniqueness in these links does not affect the numerical conclusions, or account quantitatively for its effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain treatment of multiplicities / many Θ-objects
rubrics_metrics.description: Address the fact that there are many concrete Θ-pilot objects (for j = 1,...,(ℓ−1)/2): either pick a canonical diagonal embedding, form appropriate averages, or otherwise justify how these multiplicities are handled when extracting single numerical invariants like arithmetic degrees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The authors point out that Mochizuki does not clearly resolve the multiplicity issue; any valid proof must show how to pass from many concrete objects to the single numbers used in inequalities without introducing uncontrolled errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Validity of applying anabelian reconstructions and rigidity arguments
rubrics_metrics.description: When invoking anabelian results (e.g., reconstructing curves from π_1(X) and related monoids), show that no extra automorphisms or non-geometric identifications creep in that would invalidate identifications of numerical data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholze–Stix observe that in the strictly Belyi-type situations at hand the anabelian functor is fully faithful and geometry and group theory are equivalent; a valid use of anabelian geometry must therefore either exploit genuine non-anabelian phenomena or explain why the anabelian equivalences do not trivialize/alter the required arithmetic identifications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track and justify all error terms and asymptotics (e.g., O(h^{1/2}), β_d(ℓ)·ℓ)
rubrics_metrics.description: Every approximation and inequality must come with explicit error terms and asymptotic control: e.g., justify O(h(P)^{1/2}) remainders, show α_d(ℓ)→0 as ℓ→∞, and ensure β_d(ℓ) grows at most as claimed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In reductions from heights to deg(q_E) and in the final passage to Vojta one must uniformly control small-height and exceptional cases (using e.g., Faltings finiteness), and show error terms can be absorbed into the O(1) constant or handled uniformly across the family.

rubrics_metrics.name: Demonstrate that multiradial algorithm yields concrete identifications up to controlled indeterminacy
rubrics_metrics.description: If the multiradial algorithm (IUTT-3, Theorem 3.11) is used to move from abstract pilot data to concrete pilot data, prove that it produces identifications of concrete Θ- and q-pilot objects with indeterminacies small enough to preserve the necessary arithmetic inequalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Scholze–Stix note that without acceptable control this step would be 'obviously false'. A rigorous proof must either eliminate the need for this step or provide quantitative theorems about the size and nature of the indeterminacies introduced by the algorithm.
